transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?
I'm here because I've been experiencing some continuous weight loss recently. It seems like my weight just keeps going down, so I decided to come in.
Have you been trying to lose weight or feeling very afraid of gaining weight, and how do you feel about your body shape right now?

Yes, I'm still trying to lose weight because the thought of gaining even a little bit absolutely terrifies me. When I look in the mirror, I just see myself looking so fat and out of shape, even though everyone else tells me I'm too thin. I really feel like I need to lose more to feel comfortable in my own skin.
Is your main concern that your whole body or weight is too large, or are you mostly preoccupied with a specific body part or feature that you think looks defective?
Honestly, I feel like my entire body is just too big and fat. But whenever I look in the mirror, specific parts like my stomach and my thighs look especially huge and completely out of proportion.
Have you been eating much less than usual or skipping meals to keep losing weight, and has your weight dropped to a level that doctors or others say is dangerously low?

Yes, I've been skipping meals and eating very little to keep my weight down, and it has been dropping. But I don't think my weight is dangerously low at all, and I feel completely fine. Everyone else is just worrying way too much over nothing.
Have you had episodes where you eat a large amount of food in a short time or made yourself vomit, used laxatives, or exercised excessively to prevent weight gain?

No, I've never done anything like binge eating, throwing up, or using laxatives. My focus is strictly on restricting my food intake and eating as little as possible to avoid gaining weight. I just try to control what I eat.

latest_inference.note: Previously the candidates were ["Anorexia Nervosa"], and based on this conversation that candidate remains the same and is further supported. The patient reports intense fear of gaining weight, persistent behavior interfering with weight gain through severe restriction/skipping meals, significant weight loss, distorted body image with seeing the whole body as fat despite others saying the patient is too thin, and poor recognition of the seriousness of the low weight. The denial of binge eating, vomiting, or laxative use does not weaken Anorexia Nervosa; it is consistent with a restricting pattern. No new evidence suggests another diagnosis from the allowed list more strongly than Anorexia Nervosa.

They also minimize the seriousness of their low weight. No binge eating or purging behaviors were reported, supporting anorexia nervosa, restricting pattern.
